note: 3-5 candidate geological hypotheses ranked by expected DTI improvement and implementation cost. Rank #1 was executed as Experiment 1 (this session); ranks 2-5 are deferred. No submission slot is spent on any of them.

candidates.hypothesis: Off-catalogue geothermal-relevant faults concentrate close to, but not on, USGS/INGENIOUS mapped traces, where blind splays and step-overs lack mapped traces but retain proximity propensity.
candidates.physical_signature: Inverse-distance proximity to fold-visible catalogue faults, binary top-k dots per quadrant, zeros outside the footprint.
candidates.why_it_catches_uncatalogued_faults: Blind splays, step-overs and geothermal conduits commonly lie adjacent to mapped traces without independent surface expression; a proximity band targets off-catalogue pixels near mapped structures while the pixel-exact catalogue mask avoids crediting the mapped traces themselves.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Alluvial-fan and playa depositional edges, Pleistocene pluvial Lake Lahontan wave-cut benches, and buried basalt flow margins produce distance-to-fault anomalies without Quaternary throw.
candidates.how_it_differs_from_repo_lanes: Not a deletion-pruning of the H19-5/D2.8/B1/B2 family (GEMSDOE24/25/27/28/30/31/32/33/36); no prior-prediction pixels are reused. Unlike WBG-C1 it emits off-catalogue dots from a simple geometric rule instead of a continuous Hessian commutator. Unlike WBG-2 it is distance-banded, not random scatter. Unlike WBG-3 it uses no 19-band geophysical stack, no 1 m LiDAR and no 10 m DEM derivatives.
candidates.expected_dti_improvement: Low-to-moderate; expected below the current local benchmark (10 m-3DEP S3DEP1 HOLDOUT-DTI 0.166060).
candidates.implementation_cost: Low — shared cached stack, buffered whole-component holdout, pooled DTI (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel); runs in minutes on CPU.
candidates.data_readiness: All inputs present locally (owner mirrors; hash-pinned, not independently organizer-authenticated).
candidates.result: HOLDOUT-DTI 0.012516, 95% CI [0.009511, 0.015708], n=60,988 withheld positives; leakage canary max AUC 0.613 < 0.90 (pass); registry: Spearman ≈ 0 vs r13-lattice and GEMSDOE32 B2 (passes rho <= 0.90), but forward 3-px overlap 1.0 vs r13-lattice-s5 (>70% STOP) and vs B2 0.159. Verdict negative: DO NOT SUBMIT. File: docs/downloads/wbg4-offcatalogue-proximity-from-visible-faults-zeros.tif (SHA-256 24bc089e…), run card: evidence/wbg4/run_card.json.

candidates.hypothesis: Blind, alteration-controlled geothermal faults sit at radiometric clay caps (high K/Th, low magnetite) coincident with planform/strain saddles in the DEM, even where no scarp is mapped.
layers: USGS GeoDAWN radiometrics (K, Th, U, TC; DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ)
19-band numerical features stack (cond_surf, iso_grav_anom, det_elev, elev)
OpenEI GDR submission 1391 orphan thermal wells/springs/vents (DOI 10.15121/1881483)
candidates.physical_signature: Coincident radiometric clay-cap anomaly + DEM curvature/strain saddle; optional thermal-well proximity corroboration.
candidates.why_it_catches_uncatalogued_faults: Hydrothermal alteration and blind faults need no Quaternary scarp; USGS/INGENIOUS maps subaerial traces and misses covered/alteration-controlled structures.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Paleo-channel and lacustrine clay caps, sedimentary facies changes, and non-tectonic topography saddles.
candidates.how_it_differs_from_repo_lanes: WB G-3 PPDR arm already tests magnetite-destruction residuals; this adds radiometric composition + saddle geometry and thermal-well corroboration, not yet implemented in this repo.
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium — requires original 19-band layer semantics verification (band `tc` and depth-surface interpretation are ambiguous in mirror materials; do not claim physical units).
candidates.data_readiness: GeoDAWN radiometrics public (USGS DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ); 19-band stack owner mirror present locally but hash-proven only, not organizer-authenticated.
candidates.blocker: Verify band semantics and coverage before implementing; do not claim heat/permeability/vent discovery from descriptors.

candidates.hypothesis: Concealed basin-range fault fronts produce potential-field horizontal-gradient worms aligned with mountain-range fronts, detectable without any surface scarp.
candidates.physical_signature: Horizontal-gradient magnitude worms (amplitude-invariant to remanent magnetization/inclination), skeletonized and thresholded off-catalogue.
candidates.why_it_catches_uncatalogued_faults: Magnetized basement offset across blind faults creates gradient anomalies even where alluvium covers the trace.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, dikes, and intrusive edges produce identical gradient worms.
candidates.how_it_differs_from_repo_lanes: Related to WBG-3 PPDR magnetite-destruction arm but uses total-field horizontal gradient directly rather than gravity-minus-pseudogravity residuals; not implemented in this repo.
candidates.data_readiness: Owner-mirror bands present locally; semantics unverified.

candidates.status: DEFERRED — external-data gate (NOT obtainable in this sandbox)
candidates.hypothesis: Creeping geothermal faults across zero-relief playas produce Sentinel-1 DInSAR line-of-sight velocity-gradient discontinuities invisible to 1 km GPS interpolation.
layers: NASA ASF OPERA L3 Sentinel-1 surface-displacement products, resampled to the 100 m UTM 11N grid
candidates.physical_signature: Strain-axis-projected phase-gradient discontinuity (InSAR creep gradient) across playas.
candidates.why_it_catches_uncatalogued_faults: Aseismic creep on blind faults leaves no mapped trace; InSAR sees mm/yr motion directly.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Seasonal playa groundwater pumping subsidence bowls.
candidates.how_it_differs_from_repo-lanes: Not implemented anywhere in this repo; WBG-S2/H1/WBG-3 all use LiDAR/DEM/geophysics, no InSAR.
candidates.expected_dti_improvement: Unquantified; potentially high for blind creep structures.
candidates.implementation_cost: High — requires resampling, phase unwrapping quality control, and vel-gradient computation.
candidates.data_readiness: Official free source: NASA/JPL ASF OPERA (https://asf.alaska.edu/datasets/daac/opera/). NOT obtainable in this sandbox — outbound network allowlist blocks asf.alaska.edu. Check obtainability before proposing as viable.

candidates.hypothesis: Sub-meter LiDAR curvature and 10 m 3DEP scarp/openness catch degraded <1 m range-front splays missed by the Quaternary catalogue.
layers: 1 m DEM links (DrivenData data tab, login required); 10 m USGS 3DEP DEM derivatives
candidates.physical_signature: Curvature + anti-piedmont topographic openness / LRM scarps.
candidates.why_it_catches_uncatalogued_faults: Degraded scarps under alluvial veneer may still show sub-meter curvature signatures absent from mapped traces.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Road cuts, railroad embankments, and agricultural terraces.
candidates.how_it_differs_from_repo_lanes: WBG-S2 and WBG-H1 already rely on 1 m LiDAR and peer 10 m DEM derivatives; both lanes remain stopped on the literal registry gate, so repeating the same inputs is not a path to a unique submission.
candidates.expected_dti_improvement: Already reflected in stopped WBG-S2/H1 results (0.1836 / 0.1233 HOLDOUT-DTI); no new upside without new inputs.
candidates.data_readiness: 1m_DEM_links.csv is behind the DrivenData login redirect; not obtainable without authenticated access. No credentials stored or requested.
